displayedInputs.question:
A unit hexagram is composed of a regular hexagon of side length \(1\) and its \(6\) equilateral triangular extensions, as shown in the diagram. What is the ratio of the area of the extensions to the area of the original hexagon?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Sets \(A\) and \(B,\) shown in the Venn diagram, have the same number of elements. Their union has \(2007\) elements and their intersection has \(1001\) elements. Find the number of elements in \(A.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Amanda Reckonwith draws five circles with radii \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4\) and \(5.\) Then for each circle she plots the point \((C, A),\) where \(C\) is its circumference and \(A\) is its area. Which of the following could be her graph?

What is the area of the shaded pinwheel shown in the \(5 \times 5\) grid?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

On the dart board shown in the figure below, the outer circle has radius \(6\) and the inner circle has radius \(3.\) Three radii divide each circle into three congruent regions, with point values shown. The probability that a dart will hit a given region is proportional to the area of the region. When two darts hit this board, the score is the sum of the point values of the regions hit. What is the probability that the score is odd?

[Figure 1](attached-image-9)

Older television screens have an aspect ratio of \(4:3.\) That is, the ratio of the width to the height is \(4:3.\) The aspect ratio of many movies is not \(4:3,\) so they are sometimes shown on a television screen by “letterboxing” — darkening strips of equal height at the top and bottom of the screen, as shown. Suppose a movie has an aspect ratio of \(2:1\) and is shown on an older television screen with a \(27\)-inch diagonal. What is the height, in inches, of each darkened strip?

[Figure 1](attached-image-10)

A cube with side length \(1\) is sliced by a plane that passes through two diagonally opposite vertices \(A\) and \(C\) and the midpoints \(B\) and \(D\) of two opposite edges not containing \(A\) or \(C,\) as shown. What is the area of quadrilateral \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-11)

A round table has radius \(4.\) Six rectangular place mats are placed on the table. Each place mat has width \(1\) and length \(x\) as shown. They are positioned so that each mat has two corners on the edge of the table, these two corners being end points of the same side of length \(x.\) Further, the mats are positioned so that the inner corners each touch an inner corner of an adjacent mat. What is \(x?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-12)

mappings.rationale: Joining the regular hexagon's center to its vertices partitions it into six unit equilateral triangles. Comparing these pieces with the six triangular extensions determines the area ratio without calculating individual areas.
mappings.answerReason: Each extension is congruent to one of the six equilateral triangles inside the hexagon. Both regions therefore have area equal to six such triangles, giving 1:1.

mappings.rationale: The task directly uses the cardinality formula for the union of two finite sets, accounting for their intersection being counted twice in the sum of their sizes.
mappings.answerReason: Since |A|=|B|, the union formula gives 2007=2|A|-1001. Thus |A|=(2007+1001)/2=1504.

mappings.rationale: Eliminating the radius from the circumference and area formulas gives a positive quadratic relationship between the plotted coordinates. The correct graph must increase with increasing upward curvature, rather than linearly.
mappings.answerReason: C=2πr and A=πr² imply A=C²/(4π). For radii 1 through 5, circumference increases in equal steps while area increases by 3π, 5π, 7π, and 9π. Choice A shows this increasing, upward-curving pattern.

mappings.rationale: The shaded pinwheel can be decomposed into four equal blades, each split into two triangles whose bases and perpendicular heights can be read from the grid.
mappings.answerReason: Draw a segment from the central point to each blade's inward corner. Each blade becomes two triangles with base 1 and height 1.5, so its area is 2×(1×1.5/2)=1.5. Four blades have area 6.

mappings.rationale: Sector and annular-sector areas determine the probability of each score parity. An odd total requires the mutually exclusive odd-even or even-odd outcomes, whose probabilities are multiplied for independent throws and then added. The six displayed regions are not equally likely.
mappings.answerReason: Each inner sector has area 3π and each outer region has area 9π. The regions labeled 1 have total area 3π+2×9π=21π out of 36π, so P(odd)=7/12 and P(even)=5/12. Under independent throws, the required probability is 2×(7/12)×(5/12)=35/72.
limitations: Independence of the two dart throws is implicit rather than explicitly stated; the result uses the standard independent-throw interpretation.

mappings.rationale: The screen's aspect ratio expresses its width and height as 4t and 3t. Its diagonal determines the scale through the Pythagorean theorem, after which the movie's aspect ratio determines the unused height.
mappings.answerReason: A 4t by 3t screen has diagonal 5t, so t=27/5=5.4. Its width is 21.6 and height is 16.2. The full-width 2:1 movie has height 10.8, leaving each strip with height (16.2-10.8)/2=2.7.

mappings.rationale: The requested section area reduces to planar area relationships. Right triangles on the cube's faces determine the section's equal sides and its diagonals. One can recognize a rhombus and use its diagonal formula, or split along BD and calculate two isosceles-triangle areas.
mappings.answerReason: Each section side has squared length 1²+(1/2)²=5/4, so ABCD is a rhombus. AC is a body diagonal of length √3, while BD is a diagonal of the unit square halfway up the cube, of length √2. Its area is AC×BD/2=√6/2. Equivalently, the two triangles on base BD each have height √3/2.

mappings.rationale: The touching inner edges form the regular hexagon shown, with side x and apothem √3x/2. Adding the mat width gives the distance from the center to an outer chord. The radius, this distance, and half the chord form a right triangle, producing a quadratic that can be solved by either listed method.
mappings.answerReason: The radius equation is (x/2)²+(1+√3x/2)²=16, which simplifies to x²+√3x-15=0. Its only positive root is (-√3+√63)/2=(3√7-√3)/2.
